Regenerate

/ree-JEN-uh-rayt/ · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Regenerate means to grow back lost or damaged parts, or to give new life to something in decline

Regenerate means to grow back lost or damaged parts, or to bring new life to something in decline. A young sea star can regenerate an entire arm within a year of losing it.

Worked Example

Two summers after the wildfire swept the ridge, rangers found the burned slopes beginning to regenerate, with seedlings and wildflowers pushing up through the ash.

The fire destroyed the plant life, and now new growth is replacing what was lost, the forest is literally producing itself again. Replacing what was destroyed with fresh, living growth is the heart of regenerate.

How Regenerate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

regrow

regrow: to grow again after loss

renew

renew: to make fresh or effective again

revitalize

revitalize: to give new energy and life to

Antonyms

degenerate

degenerate: to decline or decay over time

wither

wither: to shrivel, weaken, and fade

How Strong Is It? — recover → regenerate → resurrect

recover vs. regenerate

recover vs. regenerate: Recover is weaker than regenerate, an injured player recovers by healing what is hurt, while a creature that can regenerate grows back what was lost entirely.

resurrect vs. regenerate

resurrect vs. regenerate: Resurrect is stronger than regenerate, a damaged forest regenerates new growth over time, while to resurrect something is to bring it back after it has died completely.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: again

Root — gener

Root — gener: to produce, to give birth (from Latin generare)

Suffix — -ate

Suffix — -ate: to make, to cause

Put it together

Put it together: Again plus produce plus make: to regenerate is to cause something to be produced again, whether that is new tissue on a wound or new energy in a fading neighborhood.

Use the root in a new word: generator

Use the root in a new word: generator: When the power failed, the backup generator produced enough electricity to keep the whole clinic running.

Root Check

Word Choice

Neutral / scientific

Frequent in biology, as in regenerate tissue or cells, and used figuratively for places and institutions, as in efforts to regenerate a neighborhood. Do not confuse it with rejuvenate, which means to make something feel younger or fresher; regenerate implies actually growing back or producing anew what was lost.
